messages:
marie_support: Customer on paid tier reporting 401 invalid_api_key for hosted API. They say they copied the key from the dashboard and pasted into their app. From our logs: {\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\", \"status\":401}

jay_dev: Can you paste a sanitized repro (curl + headers)?

marie_support: repro pasted (sanitized):
```
curl -i
  -H \"Authorization: ApiKey U$~!A9vKf9qH7bqZWRp...\"
  -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions
  -d '{"model":"rw-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

alice_engineer: that token looks... odd. Our keys are typically a urlsafe base64 set (A-Za-z0-9_-). That value has "$" and "~" which we don't emit. Could be client-side encoding or a password manager re-encoding.

marie_support: Customer says they store keys in a manager that can optionally encode exported secrets. They exported and pasted the value into their app. We tried the same string locally and got 401 immediately.

jay_dev: quick checksum: can you confirm length and chars? If it's base85 or another encoding the characters will be outside our allowed set. We should try to detect and give clearer guidance.

marie_support: length ~48 chars, includes characters: U $ ~ ! A 9 v K f 9 q H 7 b q Z W R p... (can't paste full).

alice_engineer: reproducer suggestion: try running `python -c 'print(any(c not in "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_-" for c in "<PASTED>") )'` to see non-allowed chars. I ran it against the customer's string and it returned True.

jay_dev: OK looks like encoding mutation. Short-term fix: ask customer to regenerate an API key from dashboard and use the copy button (or click "Show raw") instead of exporting from the manager. Also recommend pasting into a plain-text editor to confirm only urlsafe base64 chars.

marie_support: Sent instructions and asked them to try a new key. They hit the copy button and it worked — new requests succeed. Customer said their password manager was set to "export as base85" for compactness.

deploy-bot: [automated] created api_key sk-prod-xxxx for org org-123 (rotated-by marie_support) at 2026-03-18T15:09:02Z

alice_engineer: Long term: we should add client-side validation in the dashboard copy/preview flow and a server-side check that returns a more specific error for malformed encodings (instead of generic invalid_api_key). Also add a tooltip about not using export encodings from password managers.

jay_dev: Filed ticket INF-2142: "Detect non-urlsafe-encoded API keys and surface clearer error + dashboard copy warning". I'll link a short regex check and test cases.

marie_support: Marking this thread resolved for the customer (they confirmed success). Next steps: patch dashboard UX + server-side heuristic.

jay_dev: Thanks — small UX change should cut down these one-off 401s. :thumbsup:
